text:
customer-jane: Hey team — around 02:00 UTC our service started returning mangled JSON from Redwood. We didn't change prompts or keys. trace_id: trc-9842. Output has odd tokenization ("\u0000" chars, escaped pieces). Auth/keys OK, latency spiked too.

sarah: Sorry about that. Can you paste a minimal repro (prompt + curl) and tell us the region you were targeting?

customer-jane: Repro below. Target was eu-west-1. We pin model to "redwood/7b-v2" in our code.

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/7b-v2","input":"{\"name\": \"Alice\", \"age\": 30}", "max_tokens": 64, "trace_id": "trc-9842"}'
```

Response we got (trimmed):

```json
{"id":"resp_...","model":"redwood/3b-q8","output":"{\u0000\"name\u0000\": \"Alice\", \"age\": 30}\n"}
```

customer-jane: Note model in response is wrong (3b) and tokenizer slipped (\u0000 bytes).

miguel: Thanks, that's very helpful. I see last log entry for trc-9842 at our gateway: 

```
2026-11-07T02:00:12Z [gateway] trace=trc-9842 client=acct-349 region=eu-west-1 target_model=redwood/7b-v2 route=auto_failover fallback_variant=redwood/3b-q8 reason=capacity_pressure
```

miguel: Gateway auto-fell back to redwood/3b-q8 due to capacity in eu-west-1 and routed to us-west-2 pool. That explains cross-region latency and model swap.

arjun: The big issue is the tokenizer/vocab mismatch between 7b-v2 and 3b-q8. They are different model groups with incompatible tokenizers; KV cache and decoding assume different token ids -> garbled tokens (\u0000).

arjun: Short-term workaround: set the request header "Accept-Fallback": "false" or include "fallback_policy": {"allow": false} to avoid silent substitution. Example: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/7b-v2","input":"hello","fallback_policy":{"allow":false},"trace_id":"trc-9842-no-fb"}'
```

infra-bot: [AUTO] failover_event trc-9842: fallback_variant=redwood/3b-q8 location=us-west-2 reason=capacity_pressure route_policy=auto_failover

nate: We're also seeing retries from the client leading to doubled token billing for this trace. billing-bot, ping.

billing-bot: Noted. Usage spike for acct-349 starting 2026-11-07T02:00:08Z. We'll open a billing review if the customer requests credits; please attach correlation traces.

customer-jane: Is there a way to force same-variant-only routing so we never get a smaller model? We need deterministic outputs for QA.

arjun: Two options: 1) Use `fallback_policy.allow=false` as above (immediate stop with 409 if cannot route). 2) For hosted customers we can enable `model_group_pin: redwood/7b` on the account so routing will only use variants compatible with the 7b tokenizer. Option 2 requires a config change by infra and is safer for production.

sarah: We'll enable model_group_pin for acct-349 for the short term. miguel, can you confirm capacity implications?

miguel: I'll coordinate with capacity team. Also adding a runtime check to reject fallback when tokenizers mismatch (instead of silent substitution) — filing ENG-RUNTIME-1427.

oncall-ml: FYI this pattern is recurring when autoscaling evicts large-variant pools. Need to add metadata to kernel selection: `tokenizer_sha` -> if mismatch then fail early. I'll take ownership of the detection rule.

arjun: Repro steps for eng/runtime to reproduce locally:
1) Pin request to model redwood/7b-v2 with trace_id trc-dup.
2) Simulate eu-west-1 capacity reduction and make gateway respond with fallback redwood/3b-q8.
3) Observe tokenizer decode errors and corrupt unicode (\u0000).

Example script (pseudo):
```python
# set env to simulate forced fallback
os.environ['SIMULATE_FALLBACK']='redwood/3b-q8'
resp = client.generate(model='redwood/7b-v2', input='{"name":"Bob"}', trace_id='trc-dup')
print(resp)
```

miguel: For immediate customer remediation: we've enabled `model_group_pin` and added the fallback_policy header as a recommended config. Also routing logs show no auth issues; the errors are purely routing/fallback.

sarah: Customer notified of workaround and next steps. Assigning to ENG-RUNTIME-1427 and CAPACITY-764.

customer-jane: Thanks team — the workaround prevented new errors. Please keep me posted on the detection rule so we can safely rely on host fallback in the future. :pray:

nate: Closing loop: created ticket SUP-2119 (customer acct-349) and linked traces trc-9842 + trc-9842-no-fb.

miguel: I'll post updates here after capacity changes.

sarah: Thanks everyone.
